# Playable MIDI instruments (Note On / Note Off) — Intake Brief

**Work Item:** TF-0MV9PIBNV008C00R | **Type:** epic | **Priority:** Medium

> **Headline:** A new `instruments` capability: purpose-crafted, polyphonic
> instruments defined as ToneGraph-shaped presets (oscillator + ADSR envelope
> + optional filter), driven live by a structured Note On / Note Off message
> API (`instrument.noteOn(note, velocity)` / `instrument.noteOff(note)`) on a
> deterministic, sample-accurate voice engine that runs in both the browser
> (Web Audio) and Node (`node-web-audio-api`).

## Problem statement

ToneForge plays fixed, one-shot sound events; there is no way to *play a
pitch* — to hold a voice while a key is down, change pitch per note, and
release it when the key lifts. MIDI Note On / Note Off is the natural way to
express that, and today nothing in the codebase maps a MIDI note number to a
live, sustained, re-triggerable sound. This item adds a family of playable
instruments plus the engine to drive them from a simple programmatic
Note On / Note Off API, so interactive and melodic use cases (game music,
prototyping, sound-design auditioning) no longer need to pre-render every
pitch.

## Users

- **Game developers / composers** prototyping interactive music or melodic
  SFX who want to trigger pitched voices expressively (note + velocity, held
  and released) without a DAW.
- **Sound designers** auditioning a ToneGraph patch across the full pitch
  range and different velocities before committing it to a library entry.
- **ToneForge maintainers** who need instruments to follow the same
  deterministic, seeded, tested conventions as the rest of the platform.

Example user stories:

- As a developer, I want `instrument.noteOn(60, 100)` then
  `instrument.noteOff(60)` to produce a sustained tone that starts on note 60
  (middle C), stays audible until the note-off, then releases — so I can play
  chords and melodies from game logic.
- As a composer, I want to hold multiple notes at once (e.g. a 3-note chord)
  and have the engine respect a voice limit with sensible stealing, so my
  usage stays predictable and CPU-safe.
- As a sound designer, I want each instrument preset to declare its own
  attack/decay/sustain/release so plucks behave differently from pads, and I
  want velocity to change loudness naturally.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Instrument note API:** each instrument exposes `noteOn(midiNote,
  velocity)` and `noteOff(midiNote)` backed by structured `midiNoteOn` /
  `midiNoteOff` message types; the engine maps MIDI notes to frequencies via
  the A4 (note 69) = 440 Hz equal-tempered formula (assertable: note 60 →
  261.63 Hz, note 69 → 440 Hz) and maps velocity (1–127) to gain.
- **ADSR envelope:** each instrument's envelope has attack / decay / sustain /
  release stages; Note On runs attack→decay→sustain-hold, Note Off runs
  release; an offline-render test asserts a held note produces non-silent
  audio during sustain and decays to silence after release.
- **Polyphony + voice management:** the engine is polyphonic with a
  configurable maximum-voice limit and a documented voice-stealing policy at
  the limit; re-triggering a note already sounding steals/replaces that
  note's own voice; tests cover chords at/over the limit and same-note
  retrigger.
- **Instrument family:** at least five instrument presets (e.g. pluck, pad,
  bass, bell, string-like lead) are defined, schema-valid, registered and
  discoverable, and each renders deterministic, non-silent audio for a given
  seed (offline render snapshot test).
- **Dual runtime:** rendering works in Node (real-time via
  `node-web-audio-api` and offline via `OfflineAudioContext`) and in the
  browser (real-time Web Audio; the existing web bundle builds without
  Node-specific imports).
- **Determinism:** same seed + same note/velocity sequence ⇒ identical output
  (byte-identical offline WAV), consistent with the platform's
  determinism guarantees.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope stays at the programmatic API** (decision Q1 = A): no raw MIDI byte
  decoder, no Web MIDI API hardware binding, and no MIDI file playback in this
  item — those are follow-ups.
- **New instrument definitions only** (decision Q2 = A): do not retrofit a
  recipe-as-instrument wrapper in this item; hand-crafted instrument presets
  first.
- Instruments must follow platform conventions: deterministic given seed,
  ToneGraph-shaped YAML/TS definitions, schema-validated, unit- and
  integration-tested, UK English.
- No changes to existing recipe/stack/sequence/CLI behaviour unless required
  for registration/discovery.
- Voice limits and stealing must be implemented in an injectable, unit-testable
  engine (like the mixer's voice tracking), not baked into the audio path.

## Existing state

- No MIDI or instrument support anywhere; `STACK_PRD.md` lists "MIDI
  sequencing" as a non-goal of the stack module.
- `src/sequence/` schedules SFX events over time (not pitched, held voices);
  `src/runtime/` loops whole rendered events with iteration-granular parameter
  changes — neither handles sample-accurate per-note voices.
- ToneGraph rendering (`src/core/tonegraph*.ts`, `src/core/renderer.ts`) and
  recipe YAML presets (`presets/recipes/*.yaml`) generate one-shot, mostly
  fixed-pitch audio; 77 of 100+ recipes already use oscillators.
- `src/audio/web-audio.ts` abstracts Web Audio for Node (`node-web-audio-api`
  installed) and browser; `web/src/audio.ts` already creates a real-time
  `AudioContext` in the browser.
- `src/mixer/runtime.ts` already tracks active voices per group
  (`maxVoices` / `activeVoices`) — a precedent for voice-limit policy.

## Desired change

- Add an `src/instruments/` module: instrument schema + validation, a
  `noteOn`/`noteOff` API with `midiNoteOn`/`midiNoteOff` message types and
  note→Hz / velocity→gain mapping, an ADSR envelope engine, a voice manager
  (polyphony, limit, stealing, same-note retrigger), and a deterministic
  renderer wired to both Node and browser Web Audio.
- Ship a starter family of 5+ instrument presets (pluck, pad, bass, bell,
  string-like lead), schema-validated and discoverable alongside the recipe
  library.
- Expose testing hooks (injectable clock, context, seed) so all behaviour is
  unit-testable; add offline-render snapshot tests for pitch, sustain,
  release, polyphony and determinism.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/instruments/schema.ts` — instrument definition schema (oscillator +
  ADSR + optional filter) and validation.
- `src/instruments/instrument.ts` — `Instrument` interface, `noteOn` /
  `noteOff`, `midiNoteOn` / `midiNoteOff` message types, note→Hz and
  velocity→gain mapping.
- `src/instruments/envelope.ts` — ADSR stage state machine (attack/decay/
  sustain/release).
- `src/instruments/voice-manager.ts` — polyphonic voice allocation, limit,
  stealing, same-note retrigger.
- `src/instruments/engine.ts` — deterministic voice renderer for Node
  (real-time + offline) and browser (real-time).
- `src/instruments/index.ts` — public exports and instrument registry.
- `src/instruments/presets/*` (or `presets/instruments/*.yaml`) — the starter
  instrument family (pluck, pad, bass, bell, string-like lead).
- `src/instruments/*.test.ts` — unit tests (mapping, envelope, polyphony,
  determinism) mirroring `src/recipes/*.test.ts` conventions.
- `docs/modules/instruments.md` (or equivalent module-index entry) — module
  documentation; README entry.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: real-time Web Audio in headless/CI environments.** *Mitigation:*
  inject `AudioContext`/`OfflineAudioContext`; tests use offline rendering
  unless a real-time context is explicitly required.
- **Risk: ambiguous voice-stealing policy** leads to surprising behaviour.
  *Mitigation:* document and unit-test the policy (e.g. steal the oldest
  sounding voice first; same-note retrigger replaces its own voice);
  configurability where reasonable.
- **Risk: scope creep** towards DAW-like features (pitch bend, CC,
  aftertouch, Web MIDI hardware, MIDI files, velocity curves, more
  instruments). *Mitigation:* recorded as explicit follow-up items, not this
  scope.
- **Risk: determinism drift from sample-rate/exception paths.** *Mitigation:*
  fixed 44100 Hz for snapshots; assert byte-identical offline output; reuse
  platform seed conventions.
- **Risk: browser/Node import split** (Node-only `node-web-audio-api` imports
  leaking into the web bundle). *Mitigation:* keep Web Audio access behind
  `src/audio/web-audio.ts`, matching the existing pattern and bundle tests.
- **Assumption:** note velocity maps monotonically to gain (linear or
  per-instrument curve) — exact curve decided in implementation with tests.
- **Assumption:** a starter family of five instruments plus the engine is the
  right first slice; the family can grow via follow-up items.

## Related work (manual)

- `Tier 4 -- Melodic Motifs (TF-0MUYBDNKI001IHW4)` — precedent for pitched
  oscillator recipes, but fixed-pitch one-shots; informs instrument preset
  craft.
- `Tier 7 -- Multi-voice Stings (TF-0MUYBDONM008UGQW)` — multi-voice
  precedent.
- `Runtime Features (TF-0MM4OWRQ70IWEKZ2)` and `Runtime session: continuous
  footsteps transport (TF-0MUYF87JH0089VQO)` — the start/stop continuous
  transport is the closest existing analog to Note On/Note Off sustain.
- `Mixer voice limiting tests (TF-0MMLC8SQ302DVYOZ)` — voice-limit precedent
  for the voice manager.
- `Web-Based Single-Sound Editor (TF-0MUTZ4TOY003DJ45)` — browser Web Audio
  real-time playback precedent.
- `docs/prd/SEQUENCER_PRD.md` — explicit boundary: the sequencer stays an
  SFX event scheduler; instruments are a distinct, complementary capability.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (playback surface / MIDI interpretation).** What should "played by
  sending MIDI Note On / Note Off" mean at the interface level?
  (A) programmatic Note On/Off API + structured message types driving real-time
  browser and Node; (B) A + raw MIDI byte decoder; (C) A/B + Web MIDI API
  hardware binding; (D) A/B + offline MIDI file playback.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **A — programmatic API only**.
    No byte decoder, hardware binding or MIDI-file playback in this item
    (recorded as follow-ups).
- **Q2 (instrument set / definition).** Where do the instruments come from?
  (A) new ToneGraph-shaped instrument definitions (oscillator + ADSR +
  optional filter) shipped as a preset family; (B) wrap existing recipes as
  instruments; (C) hybrid.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **A — new instrument
    definitions**, a purpose-crafted preset family first.
- **Q3 (polyphony / envelope semantics).** (A) polyphonic with configurable
  voice limit + stealing, per-note ADSR, Note Off → release, retrigger
  replaces the same note's voice; (B) monophonic; (C) polyphonic unlimited.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **A — polyphonic with a
    configurable voice limit and stealing, per-note ADSR, retrigger stealing
    the same note's voice.**

# Instrument test harness and offline fixtures

**Parent:** TF-0MV9PIBNV008C00R (Playable MIDI instruments)
**Type:** task (test infrastructure)

## Goal

Provide the shared, deterministic test utilities every instrument feature
depends on, so notes, envelopes, polyphony and presets can be asserted
reproducibly without ad-hoc test code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A reusable harness (e.g. `src/instruments/__tests__/helpers.ts`) renders a
  note/velocity sequence offline at a **pinned 44100 Hz** sample rate and
  returns the rendered `Float32Array` samples.
- The harness exposes analysis helpers used by later features: RMS / peak
  amplitude, silence detection, and dominant-frequency estimation (zero-crossing
  or DFT peak, within a documented tolerance).
- A smoke test proves the harness itself is deterministic (two identical runs
  produce identical output) and that analysis helpers behave correctly on
  synthetic tones (e.g. a generated 440 Hz sine reports ~440 Hz, a quiet buffer
  is reported silent).
- No production behaviour is introduced by this item; changes are limited to
  test utilities and fixtures.
- Naming, file layout and conventions mirror the existing shared helper
  precedent (e.g. the recipe test helper `src/recipes/__tests__/helpers.ts`).

**Key Files:**

- `src/instruments/__tests__/helpers.ts` (new)
- `src/instruments/__tests__/harness.test.ts` (new)

## Notes

Depends on nothing; enables all subsequent instrument features.

# Instrument schema, message types and mapping

**Parent:** TF-0MV9PIBNV008C00R (Playable MIDI instruments)
**Type:** feature

## Goal

Define the ToneGraph-shaped instrument definition schema, the structured
`midiNoteOn` / `midiNoteOff` message types and the `noteOn` / `noteOff` API
surface, plus the note→frequency and velocity→gain mappings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/instruments/schema.ts` defines and validates an instrument definition
  (oscillator + ADSR + optional filter) and rejects malformed definitions with
  actionable error messages. Schema tests are written before implementation.
- `src/instruments/instrument.ts` defines the `Instrument` interface with
  `noteOn(midiNote, velocity)` and `noteOff(midiNote)`, plus the structured
  `MidiNoteOnMessage` / `MidiNoteOffMessage` types (note number, velocity,
  time).
- `midiNoteToFrequency(69) === 440` and `midiNoteToFrequency(60) ≈ 261.6256`
  (equal-temperament, A4 = 440 Hz), with the formula documented and
  unit-tested across the MIDI range (0–127).
- `velocityToGain(127) > velocityToGain(64) > velocityToGain(1)` (monotonic),
  endpoints documented, and out-of-range velocity handled deterministically
  (clamped or rejected — behaviour explicitly tested).
- Tests cover valid definitions, each invalid-field case, the full mapping
  range, and boundary velocities.

**Key Files:**

- `src/instruments/schema.ts` (new)
- `src/instruments/instrument.ts` (new)
- `src/instruments/schema.test.ts`, `src/instruments/instrument.test.ts` (new)

## Notes

Establishes the contract every later feature builds on. No Web Audio usage in
this item.

# ADSR envelope engine

**Parent:** TF-0MV9PIBNV008C00R (Playable MIDI instruments)
**Type:** feature

## Goal

Implement the sample-accurate ADSR envelope state machine: Note On runs
attack → decay → sustain-hold; Note Off runs release.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/instruments/envelope.ts` implements attack / decay / sustain / release
  with sample-accurate stage transitions at a supplied sample rate.
- The envelope begins at 0, rises to peak over attack, falls to the sustain
  level over decay, and holds sustain indefinitely until `release()`.
- Release begins only on `release()` (i.e. Note Off); after the release tail the
  output reaches and stays at 0.
- An offline-render test asserts a held note is non-silent during sustain and
  decays to silence within the release tail after Note Off.
- Unit tests cover zero attack, zero sustain, long release, a note released
  during attack, and sample-rate independence (44100 Hz and 48000 Hz).
- No Web Audio context is required: the envelope is a pure, unit-testable
  sample generator.

**Key Files:**

- `src/instruments/envelope.ts` (new)
- `src/instruments/envelope.test.ts` (new)

## Notes

Depends on F2 (schema/contract). Voice manager (F4) consumes this.

# Voice manager: polyphony, limit and stealing

**Parent:** TF-0MV9PIBNV008C00R (Playable MIDI instruments)
**Type:** feature

## Goal

Provide an injectable, unit-testable polyphonic voice allocator with a
configurable maximum-voice limit, a documented stealing policy, and same-note
retrigger semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/instruments/voice-manager.ts` allocates a voice on Note On, frees it on
  Note Off, and tracks the active voice count (mirroring the voice-tracking
  precedent in `src/mixer/runtime.ts`).
- `maxVoices` is configurable; when a Note On arrives at the limit, the
  documented policy steals the **oldest sounding voice first**.
- Re-triggering a note that is already sounding replaces that note's own voice —
  never creating two voices for the same note.
- Tests cover: a 3-note chord, allocation exactly at the limit, allocation over
  the limit (asserting which voices survive), note-off freeing voices for reuse,
  and same-note retrigger.
- The manager has no audio-context dependency and is fully unit-testable; the
  stealing policy is stated in a doc comment and matches the tests.

**Key Files:**

- `src/instruments/voice-manager.ts` (new)
- `src/instruments/voice-manager.test.ts` (new)

## Notes

Depends on F3 (per-voice envelope lifecycle).

# Instrument engine and note API (offline + Node)

**Parent:** TF-0MV9PIBNV008C00R (Playable MIDI instruments)
**Type:** feature

## Goal

Implement `src/instruments/engine.ts`: build instrument voices as Web Audio
nodes (oscillator + envelope gain + optional filter), drive them from
`instrument.noteOn/noteOff`, and render deterministically offline for Node
(`OfflineAudioContext`) with a Node real-time path via `node-web-audio-api`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/instruments/engine.ts` renders an instrument offline via
  `OfflineAudioContext` at a pinned sample rate, accessing Web Audio only
  through `src/audio/web-audio.ts` (no direct runtime-specific imports in the
  module).
- `instrument.noteOn(60, 100)` then `instrument.noteOff(60)` produces a
  sustained tone: the offline render is non-silent while held and silent after
  the release tail.
- The rendered fundamental frequency matches the expected note frequency within
  the harness tolerance (asserted for at least notes 60 and 69).
- Velocity changes rendered loudness monotonically (higher velocity ⇒ higher
  peak/RMS).
- A Node real-time playback path exists and is verified (runtime-guarded), using
  `node-web-audio-api`; it is exercised by an integration test or an explicit
  runtime-guarded path test.
- The audio context/clock/seed are injectable so tests are hermetic and
  deterministic.

**Key Files:**

- `src/instruments/engine.ts` (new)
- `src/instruments/index.ts` (public exports)
- `src/instruments/engine.test.ts` (new)
- `src/audio/web-audio.ts` (reuse; only if the abstraction needs an additive hook)

## Notes

Depends on F4. This is the core vertical slice: API → envelope → voices → audio.

# Determinism snapshot verification

**Parent:** TF-0MV9PIBNV008C00R (Playable MIDI instruments)
**Type:** task

## Goal

Prove the platform determinism guarantee for instruments: the same seed plus the
same note/velocity sequence produces byte-identical offline output at a pinned
sample rate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Golden output fixtures (committed WAVs or SHA-256 hashes) exist for at least
  two representative note/velocity sequences and store byte-identical output.
- A test renders the sequences twice and asserts byte-identical output
  (array equality or hash equality) at a pinned 44100 Hz frame rate.
- The golden fixtures are committed and regenerated only via a documented
  mechanism (no one-off manual updates); the regeneration command is recorded in
  the module docs produced by the documentation feature.
- The determinism test fails loudly (clear message) if output drifts from the
  golden result.
- Determinism coverage extends the same-seed-different-run and
  different-seed-different-output cases.

**Key Files:**

- `src/instruments/__tests__/determinism.test.ts` (new)
- `src/instruments/__tests__/fixtures/*.wav` or a fixture-hash registry (new)

## Notes

Depends on F5 (engine). Establishes the byte-identical guarantee AC.

  types; note→Hz and velocity→gain formulas; ADSR semantics; the configurable

**Parent:** discovered-from:TF-0MV9PIBNV008C00R (Playable MIDI instruments — intake Q1 decision A deferred this scope)

**Priority:** Medium

## Goal

Import standard `.mid` files and play their contents through the instruments engine: parse the SMF binary format into MIDI events, translate them into the engine's structured `midiNoteOn`/`midiNoteOff` messages (with tempo/ticks → seconds resolution), and render deterministically offline (Node + browser bundle-safe).

## Recommended library

**Use `midi-file` (MIT, zero-dependency, ships its own `index.d.ts`).** Decision rationale:

- **MIT licence** — compatible with ToneForge; `midi-parser-js` (GPL) and any GPL/AGPL alternatives are rejected.

- **Low-level parse ↔ write** (`MidiFile.parse(buffer)` → `header` + `tracks[].events[]`, including `noteOn`/`noteOff` deltaTime events, tempo meta and time signatures) — gives us full control over tick→seconds resolution and translation into `InstrumentEvent[]`, which is all we need since the epic already shipped the playback engine.
- `@tonejs/midi` (MIT) is a viable higher-level alternative but bundles Tone.js playback surface and a musical-model abstraction we don't need; not chosen as primary.

# CLI: instrument noteon / noteoff commands for live MIDI note playback

**Parent:** TF-0MV9PIBNV008C00R (Playable MIDI instruments — Note On / Note Off)
**Type:** feature | **Priority:** medium

## Goal

As a developer or sound designer, I want a CLI command to **demo live MIDI
note playback** with the playable instrument presets: start a note, have it
keep sounding until I stop it, and stop it by sending Note Off with the same
note number — so I can audition instruments, play chords and hold drones
without writing code or opening the web demo.

The CLI commands must follow the instrument module's Note On / Note Off
semantics exactly: **a note keeps playing until a matching Note Off is sent**
(no fixed one-shot duration unless the user asks for one).

## Proposed interface

```
tf instrument noteon <note> [--preset <name>] [--velocity <0-127>] [--length <seconds>]
tf instrument noteoff <note>
```

- `tf instrument noteon 60` — start MIDI note 60 (C4) on the default
  instrument preset. The note **continues to sound until `noteoff` is sent
  with the same note number**, even after the `noteon` process exits.
- `tf instrument noteoff 60` — stop exactly note 60. Other held notes are
  unaffected (polyphonic — chords must work).
- `--length <seconds>` on `noteon` — automatically send the matching Note Off
  after the given duration (a one-shot convenience so demos don't need a
  second command).
- `--velocity` (1–127) controls loudness; defaults to a sensible value
  (e.g. 100).
- `--preset <name>` selects an instrument from the registry (e.g. pluck, pad,
  bass, bell, lead); defaults to a documented default preset.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Sustained playback across processes:** `tf instrument noteon 60` exits
  successfully while the note keeps sounding; a later `tf instrument noteoff
  60` stops it. Assertable: two sequential invocations, note audible in
  between, silent after noteoff (integration test against a recorded/mock
  audio backend).
- **Matching note number:** `noteoff` stops only the note with the same MIDI
  note number; a chord of notes 60+64+67 still sounds if only 64 is turned
  off. Unmatched `noteoff` (note not currently held) is a graceful no-op with
  an informative message and non-zero exit code.
- **`--length` auto Note Off:** `noteon 60 --length 0.6` sends the matching
  Note Off ~0.6 s later with no second command; test asserts the note is
  released (silent after release tail) at the scheduled time.
- **Velocity mapping:** `--velocity` values within 1–127 map monotonically to
  loudness; invalid values (outside the range, non-numeric) produce a clear
  error and non-zero exit.
- **Preset selection:** `--preset` accepts any registered instrument preset;
  an unknown preset name is a clear error listing available presets.
- **Validation:** `noteon` / `noteoff` reject MIDI note numbers outside 0–127
  with a clear error and non-zero exit (reuse the existing `midiNoteOn` /
  `midiNoteOff` RangeError validation).
- **CLI surface:** `tf instrument --help` documents both subcommands and the
  `--length` / `--velocity` / `--preset` options; the top-level `tf --help`
  lists `instrument`. No existing CLI command behaviour changes.
- **Determinism / testability:** the audio engine stays behind the existing
  `createRealtimeInstrument` API (Node `node-web-audio-api`); CLI integration
  tests run headless against a harness/mock context that records
  noteon/noteoff events and their times — no physical audio device required
  in CI.
- All related documentation is updated (CLI reference, instruments module
  doc, README), and the full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **Programmatic API only is out of scope to change** — this item adds the
  CLI surface on top of the existing `createRealtimeInstrument` /
  `midiNoteOn` / `midiNoteOff` API; it does not add MIDI byte decoding, Web
  MIDI hardware binding or MIDI file playback (still recorded follow-ups).
- Sustained cross-process playback implies a persistent audio engine process
  — follow the existing long-running service precedent
  (`tf runtime start --serve`, `src/runtime/service.ts`) with clean
  shutdown; note the design choice explicitly (daemon spawned on first
  `noteon` vs. always-on service) as resolved-by-implementation.
- No changes to the web bundle; real-time Node audio stays behind
  `src/audio/web-audio.ts` / `node-web-audio-api` as today.
- UK English in all user-facing text and docs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/cli/commands/instrument.ts` (new) — `noteon` / `noteoff` subcommands.
- `src/cli.yargs.ts` — register the `instrument` command group.
- `src/instruments/engine.ts` / `src/instruments/presets.ts` — existing
  `createRealtimeInstrument`, `listInstrumentSummaries`, `midiNoteOn` /
  `midiNoteOff` reuse.
- New daemon/service and transport for cross-process sustained playback —
  pattern from `src/runtime/service.ts` and `src/runtime/runtime.ts`.
- `src/cli.instrument.integration.test.ts` (new) — headless event-recorded
  noteon/noteoff/--length assertions.
- `docs/modules/instruments.md` and CLI reference docs — update.

## Related work

- `TF-0MV9PIBNV008C00R` — parent epic; its scope boundary explicitly records
  CLI/external surfaces as follow-ups.
- `TF-0MUTZ4TOY003DJ45` — Web-Based Single-Sound Editor (browser real-time
  playback precedent).
- `TF-0MM4OWRQ70IWEKZ2` — Runtime Features (long-running live service
  precedent for the sustained-playback daemon).

# CLI: render instrument notes to WAV (--output) and one-shot fallback playback (--fallback)

**Parent:** TF-0MV9PIBNV008C00R (Playable MIDI instruments — Note On / Note Off)
**Related:** TF-0MVBECXFJ006SSW4 (CLI instrument noteon/noteoff — this is the follow-up that makes those commands work without a live audio device)
**Type:** feature | **Priority:** high

## Goal

As a user on a machine **without a live audio device** (WSL, headless/CI,
docker, or an ALSA/JACK misconfiguration), I want `tf instrument` to still
produce audio I can use:

1. **`--output <file.wav>`** — render a note (or note-off) to a deterministic
   WAV file offline, so I can play it later (`tf play out.wav`), inspect it or
   ship it.
2. **`--fallback`** — play a note through an intermediate offline pre-render
   plus the platform's existing system player (the same path `tf generate`
   uses), accepting a small start delay.

Real-time sustained playback (hold until `noteoff`) is unchanged; these flags
are additive and never required when a device is available.

## Proposed interface

```
tf instrument noteon <note> [--preset <name>] [--velocity <1-127>] [--length <seconds>] [--output <file.wav>]
tf instrument noteon <note> [--preset <name>] [--velocity <1-127>] [--length <seconds>] --fallback
```

- `--output <file.wav>` renders *this invocation's note* offline via the
  existing deterministic `renderInstrument` (note On at t=0, Note Off at
  `--length`, release tail included) and writes a valid WAV. Works with zero
  audio hardware. Without `--length`, a documented default hold (e.g. 1 s) is
  used so the render always terminates.
- `--fallback` renders the same note offline to a temp WAV and plays it via
  the system player (`src/audio/player.ts` — the same `paplay`/`aplay -D
  pulse`/`ffplay` path `tf generate` uses), so it is audible on WSL/PulseAudio
  setups where `node-web-audio-api` cannot open a device. The render/schedule
  start delay is documented.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **`--output` renders offline, no device required:** `tf instrument noteon
  60 --preset pad --length 2 --output /tmp/a.wav` exits 0 on a device-less
  machine and writes a WAV that decodes with the expected sample rate
  (44100 Hz) and a duration covering hold + release tail; the leading
  fundamental is the pitched note (assertable by the existing analysis
  helpers).
- **Determinism:** the same note/velocity/preset/length produce a
  byte-identical WAV (reuse `renderInstrument`'s guarantees; test with the
  harness compareBuffer helper).
- **Default hold:** `--output` without `--length` still renders a finite,
  documented note (default hold) — never hangs and never produces an empty
  file.
- **`--fallback` plays via the system player:** with an injected/recorded
  player, `noteon 60 --length 0.5 --fallback` renders the note and hands the
  audio to the player; headless integration test asserts the player received a
  non-silent, correctly-durationed buffer and the command exits 0 with no
  real-time device.
- **Flags are additive:** without `--output`/`--fallback` the sustained
  hold-until-noteoff behaviour of TF-0MVBECXFJ006SSW4 is unchanged; giving
  both flags is a documented error (or `--output` wins — pick and document).
- **JSON mode:** `--json` reports `{ command, note, preset, velocity, length,
  file|played, fallback, sampleRate, duration }` (machine-readable).
- **Validation:** existing note/velocity/length/preset validation applies;
  `--output` to an unwritable path is a clear error with exit 1.
- Docs updated (`toneforge instrument noteon --help`, group help,
  `docs/modules/instruments.md`), and the full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Reuse `renderInstrument`/`encodeWav`/`playAudio` — **no new synthesis
  engine** and no changes to the sample-accurate voice engine.
- Real-time path (daemon) untouched except where a shared
  note→events→render helper is extracted; any refactor must keep existing
  daemon tests green.
- UK English user-facing text.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/cli/commands/instrument.ts` — `--output` / `--fallback` handling.
- New small helper (e.g. `src/instruments/offline-demo.ts`) turning CLI
  note args into `InstrumentEvent[]` and rendering to a WAV buffer.
- `src/cli.instrument.integration.test.ts` (+ maybe a new unit file) —
  offline WAV determinism/geometry, injected-player fallback test.
- Docs: `src/cli/commands/instrument.ts` help text, `docs/modules/instruments.md`.

## Related work

- `TF-0MVBECXFJ006SSW4` — the CLI this extends; its daemon uses
  `node-web-audio-api`, which cannot open a device on WSL/headless.

# CLI: detect missing audio device / WSL and print an actionable error

**Parent:** TF-0MV9PIBNV008C00R (Playable MIDI instruments — Note On / Note Off)
**Related:** TF-0MVBECXFJ006SSW4 (CLI instrument noteon/noteoff); **depends on** the `--output` / `--fallback` flags shipped by its child feature (WSL/game of the same feature family)
**Type:** feature | **Priority:** medium

## Goal

As a user on WSL, in a container, or on any machine where real-time audio is
not set up (no ALSA card, no JACK/PipeWire, `node-web-audio-api` throws
`DeviceNotAvailable` / ALSA `Unknown PCM default`), I want `tf instrument` to
fail with a **clear, actionable message** instead of a raw cpal/ALSA
traceback, and to tell me which alternatives exist (`--output` to save a WAV,
or `--fallback` for offline pre-rendered playback with a start delay).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **WSL detection:** the CLI detects WSL (`/proc/version` containing
  "microsoft", or `WSL_DISTRO_NAME` / `WSL_INTEROP` present) and reports it.
- **Device probe:** the daemon/driver probes real-time availability exactly
  once at startup (attempting to create the real-time engine via the
  injectable factory) instead of failing mid-note with a raw error; a missing
  or unusable output device is recorded as `audioDeviceAvailable: false`.
- **Actionable error on sustained notes:** `tf instrument noteon <note>`
  (no fallback flags) when `audioDeviceAvailable` is false exits 1 and prints
  a UK-English message naming the detected environment (e.g. "WSL detected —
  no live audio device is available") and suggesting **both** alternatives:
  (a) `... --output <file.wav>` to render a WAV you can play elsewhere, or
  (b) `... --fallback` for playback via an offline pre-render (note: playback
  starts after a short render delay). No stack trace is printed.
- **`status` reports capability:** `tf instrument status --json` includes
  `{ environment, audioDeviceAvailable, notes }`; human output shows a hint
  when audio is unavailable.
- **Non-crashing metadata commands:** `status`, `stop`, `presets` and
  `noteoff --json` never crash on a missing device.
- **Tests are hermetic:** headless tests inject (i) an engine factory that
  throws `DeviceNotAvailable` and (ii) an injectable system-info source, so
  WSL/no-device behaviour is asserted without depending on the host; also
  asserts the message text contains both suggested alternatives and the exit
  code is 1 (sustained noteoff path not affected by the message).
- Docs updated (help text and `docs/modules/instruments.md` note about WSL /
  device-less usage), full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Detection must be injectable/testable — never hard-code the host platform
  into assertions.
- Error text must be UK English and actionable; no raw cpal/ALSA diagnostics
  leak to the user unless a verbose/debug flag is given.
- No behaviour change when an audio device IS available.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/instruments/daemon.ts` (or a new `src/instruments/audio-probe.ts`) —
  device probe + WSL detection (injectable).
- `src/instruments/cli.ts` / `src/cli/commands/instrument.ts` — error-message
  wiring referencing `--output` / `--fallback` (from the child feature).
- `src/cli.instrument.integration.test.ts` (+ unit test for the probe) —
  injected `DeviceNotAvailable` and WSL-info source.

## Related work

- The child feature that adds `--output` / `--fallback` (renders the exact
  alternatives this message suggests) — **must land first** so the suggested
  commands work.
- `TF-0MVBECXFJ006SSW4` — the CLI command group this improves.
